fixed_statement:
- Let \(\mu\) be the probability measure from Proposition 2.
- Let \(P_t\) be the Markov semigroup associated with the singular SPDE on \(C_0([0,1])\).

\(P_t\) has exactly one invariant probability measure on \(C_0([0,1])\).
fixed_proof: Proposition 3 gives that \(\mu\) is an invariant probability measure for \(P_t\). Lemma 4.1 gives full support of \(\mu\). Lemma 4.2 gives topological irreducibility. Lemma 4.3 gives the Gibbs and reversibility assertion. Applying Lemma 4.4 on the connected state space \(C_0([0,1])\), the process can possess at most one invariant probability measure. Since Proposition 3 supplies one, there is exactly one invariant probability measure.
